reuse.why: It threads the flag through the existing getVisibleUntemplatedCategories/setMonthAvg path, but instead of splitting the existing visibleUntemplatedCategory SQL fragment into a hidden part and the other exclusions, it swaps the whole fragment out and re-types the exclusions.

duplication.why: The #fixed and saved-template SQL conditions now exist both in the visibleUntemplatedCategory constant and inline in getVisibleUntemplatedCategories (and are applied twice on the default path); copyPreviousMonth keeps its own JS version of the same exclusion rule, and the args shape is written as MonthWideBudgetArgs and again inline for copyPreviousMonth.

placement.why: Everything stays in budget/actions.ts where the tree keeps the month-wide selection and actions.

scope.why: Focused on the flag; reordering set6MonthAvg/setMonthAvg and switching signatures to an args object is incidental churn.

maintainability.why: A future change to the template or #fixed exclusion must now be made in the constant, the inline WHERE and copyPreviousMonth, and the helper's name 'getVisibleUntemplatedCategories' no longer describes what it returns when the flag is set.

bypasses_abstraction.where: getVisibleUntemplatedCategories replaces the shared visibleUntemplatedCategory fragment with 'c.tombstone = 0' and its own copy of the other exclusions when includeHiddenCategories is set; copyPreviousMonth applies the flag in its own inline condition.

disguised_duplication.where: The #fixed/saved-template conditions from visibleUntemplatedCategory are re-indented and appended inside getVisibleUntemplatedCategories rather than factored out of the constant.

abstraction_drift.where: getVisibleUntemplatedCategories and setMonthAvg each gained an includeHiddenCategories parameter, the helper gained a visibilityFilter ternary that swaps out the shared SQL fragment, and copyPreviousMonth decides the rule (now including the flag) in its own condition.
